Using AAA authentication for interactive management access to the device provides consistent, centralized control of your network. The default under AAA (local or network) is to require users to log in using a valid user name and password. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; do not use 'show running-config all' or 'show startup-config').

title: Set 'login authentication for 'ip http'

Configure the device to enforce authentication for the HTTP server (ip http) by defining a valid login method. This ensures that only authorized users can access the device's web-based management interface. Fails only when the HTTP or HTTPS server is enabled and no 'ip http authentication' line exists; passes when both servers are disabled. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; do not use 'show running-config all' or 'show startup-config').

title: Set 'transport input ssh' for 'line vty' connections
description: Selects the Secure Shell (SSH) protocol. Configuring VTY access control restricts remote access to only those authorized to manage the device and prevents unauthorized users from accessing the system. Fails if any 'line vty' block lacks 'transport input ssh' or still allows telnet/all. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; do not use 'show running-config all' or 'show startup-config').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XE 17.x Benchmark v2.2.1 - 1.2.2 Set 'transport input ssh' for 'line vty' connections

remediation.command:
! Apply SSH to transport input on all VTY management lines
line vty <line-number> <ending-line-number>
transport input ssh

title: Create 'access-list' for use with 'line vty'
description: Access lists control the transmission of packets on an interface, control Virtual Terminal Line (VTY) access, and restrict the contents of routing updates. The Cisco IOS software stops checking the extended access list after a match occurs. VTY ACLs control what addresses may attempt to log in to the router. Configuring VTY lines to use an ACL, restricts the sources where a user can manage the device. CIS assessment: Manual. Reported as SKIP with review instructions.
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XE 17.x Benchmark v2.2.1 - 1.2.4 Create 'access-list' for use with 'line vty'

audit.command: CIS assessment: Manual. Perform the following to determine if the ACL is created: Verify the appropriate access-list definitions hostname#sh ip access-list <vty_acl_number>

remediation.command:
! Configure the VTY ACL that will be used to restrict management access to the device.
access-list <vty_acl_number> permit tcp <vty_acl_block_with_mask> any
access-list <vty_acl_number> permit tcp host <vty_acl_host> any
deny ip any any log

title: Set 'access-class' for 'line vty'
description: The 'access-class' setting restricts incoming and outgoing connections between a particular vty (into a Cisco device) and the networking devices associated with addresses in an access list. Restricting the type of network devices, associated with the addresses on the access-list, further restricts remote access to those devices authorized to manage the device and reduces the risk of unauthorized access. Fails if any 'line vty' block has no 'access-class <acl> in'. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; do not use 'show running-config all' or 'show startup-config').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XE 17.x Benchmark v2.2.1 - 1.2.5 Set 'access-class' for 'line vty'

remediation.command:
! Configure remote management access control restrictions for all VTY lines.
line vty <line-number> <ending-line-number>
access-class <vty_acl_number> in

title: Set 'exec-timeout' to less than or equal to 10 minutes 'line vty'
description: If no input is detected during the interval, the EXEC facility resumes the current connection. If no connections exist, the EXEC facility returns the terminal to the idle state and disconnects the incoming session. This prevents unauthorized users from misusing abandoned sessions. For example, if the network administrator leaves for the day and leaves a computer open with an enabled login session accessible. The 10 minute default is not shown in the config; fails only if a 'line vty' block sets a timeout above 10 minutes or disables it (0 0). Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; do not use 'show running-config all' or 'show startup-config').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XE 17.x Benchmark v2.2.1 - 1.2.8 Set 'exec-timeout' to less than or equal to 10 minutes 'line vty'

remediation.command:
! Configure device timeout (10 minutes or less) to disconnect sessions after a fixed idle time.
line vty {line_number} [ending_line_number]
exec-timeout <timeout_in_minutes> <timeout_in_seconds>

title: Set 'http Secure-server' limit
description: Device management includes the ability to control the number of administrators and management sessions that manage a device. Limiting the number of allowed administrators and sessions per administrator based on account type, role, or access type is helpful in limiting risks related to denial-of-service (DoS) attacks. This requirement addresses concurrent sessions for administrative accounts and does not address concurrent sessions by a single administrator via multiple administrative accounts. Fails when 'ip http secure-server' is enabled without an 'ip http max-connections' limit. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; do not use 'show running-config all' or 'show startup-config').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XE 17.x Benchmark v2.2.1 - 1.2.9 Set 'http Secure-server' limit

remediation.command: ip http max-connections 2

title: Set 'exec-timeout' to less than or equal to 10 min on 'ip http'
description: If no input is detected during the interval, the EXEC facility resumes the current connection. If no connections exist, the EXEC facility returns the terminal to the idle state and disconnects the incoming session. This prevents unauthorized users from misusing abandoned sessions. For example, if the network administrator leaves for the day and leaves a computer open with an enabled login session accessible. Fails when an HTTP(S) server is enabled without 'ip http timeout-policy idle', or when the idle value exceeds 600 seconds. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; do not use 'show running-config all' or 'show startup-config').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XE 17.x Benchmark v2.2.1 - 1.2.10 Set 'exec-timeout' to less than or equal to 10 min on 'ip http'

remediation.command: Configure device timeout (10 minutes or less) to disconnect sessions after a fixed idle time. ip http timeout-policy idle 600 life {nnnn} requests {nn}

title: Set 'password' for 'enable secret'
description: Use the enable secret command to provide an additional layer of security over the enable password. The enable secret command provides better security by storing the enable secret password using a nonreversible cryptographic function. The added layer of security encryption provides is useful in environments where the password crosses the network or is stored on a TFTP server. In Cisco IOS XE, password types 8 and 9 are considered more secure than older password types because they use strong hashing algorithms. - Type 8 passwords use PBKDF2 with SHA-256, which is an improvement over older MD5-based hashing methods. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; do not use 'show running-config all' or 'show startup-config').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XE 17.x Benchmark v2.2.1 - 1.4.1 Set 'password' for 'enable secret'

remediation.command:
! Configure a strong, enable secret password.
enable secret 9 {ENABLE_SECRET_PASSWORD}

title: Enable 'service password-encryption'
description: When password encryption is enabled, the encrypted form of the passwords is displayed when a more system:running-config command is entered. This requires passwords to be encrypted in the configuration file to prevent unauthorized users from learning the passwords just by reading the configuration. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; do not use 'show running-config all' or 'show startup-config').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XE 17.x Benchmark v2.2.1 - 1.4.2 Enable 'service password-encryption'

remediation.command:
! Enable password encryption service to protect sensitive access passwords in the device configuration.
service password-encryption

title: Set 'username secret' for all local users
description: Username secret password type 5 and enable secret password type 5 must be migrated to the stronger password type 8 or 9. IF a device is upgraded from IOS XE 16.9 or later the type 5 is auto converted to type 9. The username secret command provides an additional layer of security over the username password. Default device configuration does not require strong user authentication potentially enabling unfettered access to an attacker that is able to reach the device. Fails if any 'username' line is configured without 'secret'. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; do not use 'show running-config all' or 'show startup-config').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XE 17.x Benchmark v2.2.1 - 1.4.3 Set 'username secret' for all local users

remediation.command:
! Create a local user with an encrypted, complex (not easily guessed) password.
username {LOCAL_USERNAME} secret {LOCAL_PASSWORD}

title: Unset 'private' for 'snmp-server community'
description: An SNMP community string permits read-only access to all objects. The default community string "private" is well known. Using easy to guess, well known community string poses a threat that an attacker can effortlessly gain unauthorized access to the device. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; do not use 'show running-config all' or 'show startup-config').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XE 17.x Benchmark v2.2.1 - 1.5.2 Unset 'private' for 'snmp-server community'

remediation.command:
! Disable the default SNMP community string private
no snmp-server community {private}

title: Unset 'public' for 'snmp-server community'
description: An SNMP community string permits read-only access to all objects. The default community string "public" is well known. Using easy to guess, well known community string poses a threat that an attacker can effortlessly gain unauthorized access to the device. title: Do not set 'RW' for any 'snmp-server community'
description: Specifies read-write access. Authorized management stations can both retrieve and modify MIB objects. Enabling SNMP read-write enables remote management of the device. Unless absolutely necessary, do not allow simple network management protocol (SNMP) write access. CIS marks this Manual; automated here because RW communities are visible directly in the running configuration. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; do not use 'show running-config all' or 'show startup-config').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XE 17.x Benchmark v2.2.1 - 1.5.4 Do not set 'RW' for any 'snmp-server community'

! Disable SNMP write access.

title: Set the ACL for each 'snmp-server community'
description: This feature specifies a list of IP addresses that are allowed to use the community string to gain access to the SNMP agent. If ACLs are not applied, then anyone with a valid SNMP community string can potentially monitor and manage the router. An ACL should be defined and applied for all SNMP access to limit access to a small number of authorized management stations segmented in a ... CIS marks this Manual; automated here: fails if a community line ends without an ACL name or number. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; do not use 'show running-config all' or 'show startup-config').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XE 17.x Benchmark v2.2.1 - 1.5.5 Set the ACL for each 'snmp-server community'

remediation.command:
! Configure authorized SNMP community string and restrict access to authorized management systems.

title: Set 'seconds' for 'ip ssh timeout' for 60 seconds or less
description: The time interval that the router waits for the SSH client to respond before disconnecting an uncompleted login attempt. This reduces the risk of an administrator leaving an authenticated session logged in for an extended period of time. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; do not use 'show running-config all' or 'show startup-config').

! Configure the SSH timeout

title: Set maximum value for 'ip ssh authentication-retries'
description: The number of retries before the SSH login session disconnects. This limits the number of times an unauthorized user can attempt a password without having to establish a new SSH login attempt. This reduces the potential for success during online brute force attacks by limiting the number of login attempts per SSH ... The default of 3 retries is compliant and not shown; fails only if a value above 3 is configured. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; do not use 'show running-config all' or 'show startup-config').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XE 17.x Benchmark v2.2.1 - 2.1.1.1.5 Set maximum value for 'ip ssh authentication-retries'

remediation.command:
! Configure the SSH timeout: 3 or less

title: Set version 2 for 'ip ssh version'
description: Specify the version of Secure Shell (SSH) to be run on a router. SSH Version 1 has been subject to a number of serious vulnerabilities and is no longer considered to be a secure protocol, resulting in the adoption of SSH Version 2 as an Internet Standard in 2006. CIS marks this Manual; automated because the setting is a single configuration line. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; do not use 'show running-config all' or 'show startup-config').

title: Set the 'hostname'
description: The hostname is used in prompts and default configuration filenames. The domain name is prerequisite for setting up SSH. Also fails when the factory default hostname (Router/Switch) is still set. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; do not use 'show running-config all' or 'show startup-config').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XE 17.x Benchmark v2.2.1 - 2.1.1.1.1 Set the 'hostname'

remediation.command:
! Configure an appropriate host name for the router.
hostname {router_name}

title: Set the 'ip domain-name'
description: Define a default domain name that the Cisco IOS software uses to complete unqualified hostnames. The domain name is a prerequisite for setting up SSH. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; do not use 'show running-config all' or 'show startup-config').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XE 17.x Benchmark v2.2.1 - 2.1.1.1.2 Set the 'ip domain-name'

remediation.command:
! Configure an appropriate domain name for the router.
ip domain-name {domain-name}

title: Set 'service timestamps debug datetime'
description: Configure the system to apply a time stamp to debugging messages or system logging messages. Including timestamps in log messages allows correlating events and tracing network attacks across multiple devices. Enabling service timestamp to mark the time log messages were generated simplifies obtaining a holistic view of events enabling faster ... Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; do not use 'show running-config all' or 'show startup-config').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XE 17.x Benchmark v2.2.1 - 2.2.6 Set 'service timestamps debug datetime'

remediation.command:
! Configure debug messages to include timestamps.
service timestamps debug datetime {msec} show-timezone

title: Create a single 'interface loopback'
description: Configure a single loopback interface. Software-only loopback interface that emulates an interface that is always up. It is a virtual interface supported on all platforms. Alternate loopback addresses create a potential for abuse, mis-configuration, and inconsistencies. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; do not use 'show running-config all' or 'show startup-config').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XE 17.x Benchmark v2.2.1 - 2.4.1 Create a single 'interface loopback'

remediation.command:
! Define and configure one loopback interface. Below is an example
interface loopback 0
ip address 10.10.10.10 255.255.255.0

title: Set 'ntp source' to Loopback Interface
description: Use a particular source address in Network Time Protocol (NTP) packets. Set the source address to be used when sending NTP traffic. This may be required if the NTP servers you peer with filter based on IP address. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; do not use 'show running-config all' or 'show startup-config').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XE 17.x Benchmark v2.2.1 - 2.4.3 Set 'ntp source' to Loopback Interface

remediation.command:
! Bind the NTP service to the loopback interface.
ntp source loopback {loopback_interface_number}

title: Set 'ip tftp source-interface' to the Loopback Interface
description: Specify the IP address of an interface as the source address for TFTP connections. This is required so that the TFTP servers can easily identify routers and authenticate requests by their IP address. CIS marks this Manual; automated as a config-line check. Audited against the output of 'show running-config' (run 'terminal length 0' first; do not use 'show running-config all' or 'show startup-config').
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XE 17.x Benchmark v2.2.1 - 2.4.4 Set 'ip tftp source-interface' to the Loopback Interface

remediation.command:
! Bind the TFTP client to the loopback interface.
ip tftp source-interface loopback {loobpback_interface_number}

title: Set 'authentication message-digest' for OSPF area
description: Enable MD5 authentication for OSPF. This is part of the OSPF authentication setup. CIS assessment: Manual. Reported as SKIP with review instructions.
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XE 17.x Benchmark v2.2.1 - 3.3.2.1 Set 'authentication message-digest' for OSPF area

audit.command: CIS assessment: Manual. Verify message digest for OSPF is defined hostname#sh run | sec router ospf

remediation.command:
! Configure the Message Digest option for OSPF.
router ospf <ospf_process-id>
area <ospf_area-id> authentication message-digest

title: Set 'ip ospf message-digest-key md5'
description: Enable Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) Message Digest 5 (MD5) authentication. This is part of the OSPF authentication setup. CIS assessment: Manual. Reported as SKIP with review instructions.
reference: CIS Cisco IOS XE 17.x Benchmark v2.2.1 - 3.3.2.2 Set 'ip ospf message-digest-key md5'
